human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Build a small CLI tool that greets users. It should accept a --name flag, default to 'World', and print 'Hello, <name>!' to stdout. The script must be importable as a module with a pure greet(name) function. Must include a test.
human_pressure.goal: Produce a runnable, importable, tested CLI greeting script.
do_not_misread: This is a CLI entry-point script, not a library package.
The greet() function must NOT print itself — __main__ handles I/O.
red_lines: Do not touch README.md or any existing code
Use only the Python standard library

machine_core.goal: Create a CLI script at src/greet.py with a --name flag (default 'World') and a pure greet(name: str) -> str function. Include a test at tests/test_greet.py covering default, named, and edge cases.
validate: python -c "from src.greet import greet; assert greet('Bob') == 'Hello, Bob!'"
acceptance: src/greet.py exists and is importable as a module
tests/test_greet.py exists and passes all cases
red_lines: src/greet.py must not import third-party packages
greet() must not call print() or write to stdout

must_check: src/greet.py exists with a greet(name) -> str function
tests/test_greet.py covers default, named, and edge-case inputs
reject_if: greet() calls print() or writes to stdout
